title: Current groundwater forcing sign asymmetry in the allocation forecast

sequencing.rationale: Open a distinct falsification dimension after the H5-H7 memory/forecast bridge closed: equal-magnitude positive and negative current vertical forcing.

derivation: In Ribasim v2026.1.1 allocation setup, Basin drainage is explicit positive forcing on the volume-conservation RHS, whereas Basin infiltration is implicit negative forcing multiplied by low_storage_factor.
The accepted storage excess M=7.9903723811 m3 is the same in all cases and can be released to the LevelDemand target at the next allocation boundary.
With no vertical forcing, source plus accepted memory gives root allocation 32 + M = 39.9903723811 m3/day.
With negative infiltration and free alpha, H6 already qualified alpha=0, so the same accepted-memory root allocation is preserved.

With equal-magnitude positive drainage, the explicit +8.0000425122 m3 enters availability directly. Source + memory + drainage = 47.9904148933 m3/day, so root is full 40 and the priority-3 external demand receives the remaining 7.9904148933 m3/day.
hypotheses: Equal-magnitude positive and negative current groundwater forcing are not allocation-symmetric in the tested v2026.1.1 topology.
Negative infiltration remains attenuable through low_storage_factor and therefore does not reduce the H6 accepted-memory root allocation when alpha is free.
Positive drainage enters as explicit availability and raises managed allocation directly: root becomes 40 m3/day and external becomes approximately 7.9904148933 m3/day.
The accepted storage draw remains approximately 7.9903723811 m3 in all three cases, isolating forcing-sign representation rather than changing memory.
forbidden: no claim that all positive and negative Ribasim processes share these semantics
no retuning after observed H8 output
do not reinterpret sign asymmetry as a conservation violation
